blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Accurate contact modeling is fundamental to understanding hand–object interaction, yet existing contact representations are typically restricted to object surfaces and rely on hand - crafted rules to recover contact details, leading to severe penetrations and implausible results. To better exploit the rich detail in motion - capture data, we introduce Vol umetric Co ntact (VolCo), a representation that expands surface points to a set of 3D volumetric grids. VolCo encodes 3D contact that allows precise hand part recovery, and is organized in an inherent hierarchy: local contact details within each volume and global hand geometry across all volumes. Our framework, VolCoDiff, employs two modules to capture local and global features following this hierarchy. For local contact details, we use a 3D variational autoencoder to model the possible hand configurations conditioned on the local object signed distance field (SDF). For global hand geometry, we design a prior - guided diffusion model that learns the distribution of compressed latent features aggregated from the volumetric grids. We evaluate our method on two benchmark datasets and demonstrate state - of - the - art performance in penetration and stability, indicating the capability to generate tight grasps with much less severe penetrations. Our code is available at https://github.com/chzh9311/volco .

VolCo编码了允许精确手部恢复的3D接觸,并被组织成一个固有的层次:每个卷内的局部联系方式和所有卷间的全局手相几何. 我们的框架,VolCodiff,使用两个模块来捕捉按照这种等级划分的地方和全球特征。 对于本地联系方式的细节,我们使用一个3D可变自编码器来模拟以本地对象签名距离域(SDF)为条件的可能的手相配置. 就全球手相几何而言,我们设计了一种先导的传播模型,该模型学习从体积网格中汇总的压缩潜在特征的分布。 我们用两个基准数据集来评估我们的方法,并展示渗透和稳定方面的艺术表现状况,表明有能力用较不严重的渗透来产生紧凑的把握。 我们的代码可以在https://github.com/chzh9311/volco上找到. 。 。 。 。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Hands are the primary means by which we interact with our surroundings. Recently, the research community has dedicated significant attention to modeling object grasping [ 40 , 47 , 44 , 21 , 23 ] due to its broad applications in AR/VR [ 10 ] , robotics [ 22 , 41 ] , and human-computer interaction [ 12 ] .
blocks.zh: 手是我们与周围环境互动的主要手段。 最近,由于在AR/VR[10]、机器人[22]、41]和人与计算机互动[12]中的广泛应用,研究界对掌握物体[40、47、44、21、23]的模型制作给予了极大的关注。

blocks.en: As a fundamental problem in this field, human grasp generation aims to synthesize plausible human hand grasps for a given object template, where MANO [ 32 ] is used as the mainstream hand representation. MANO parameters are predicted directly [ 34 , 17 , 49 , 39 ] or fitted from 3D fields [ 19 , 43 , 27 ] or contact maps indicating the contact regions, hand part orientations, etc., [ 47 , 24 , 45 , 23 , 27 , 6 ] .
blocks.zh: 作为这个领域的一个基本问题,人类的抓取生成旨在合成一个特定对象模板的似是而非的人类手抓取,其中MANO [32]作为主流的手来表示. MANO参数直接预测[34.、17.、49.39]或从3D字段[19.、43.、27]或显示接触区域、手部取向等的联系地图上安装,[47.、24.、45.、23.、27.、6]。

blocks.en: Existing methods mostly rely on hand-crafted rules in test-time-adaptation (TTA) to control penetrations [ 11 ] . Such TTA has limited adaptivity since the rules rely on object surface shapes. As shown in Fig. 1 , penetration losses based on nearest-neighbor (NN) queries is non-robust, changing gradient directions when the point crosses the medium line. Moreover, slight penetrations are expected at contact regions with rigid models like MANO, but this method cannot control the exact penetration depth. Consequently, some generated grasps still show severe penetrations and limited plausibility.
blocks.zh: 现有方法主要依靠试验时间适应(TTA)中的手工规则来控制穿透[11]. 由于规则依赖于物体表面形状,这种TTA的适应性有限. 如图1所示,以近邻查询(NN)为基础的穿透损失为非robust,当点越过中线时会改变梯度方向. 此外,在像MANO这样的刚性模型相接的区域,预计会有轻微穿透,但这种方法无法控制精确穿入深度. 因此,一些生成的抓取仍然显示出严重的渗透和有限的可信度。

blocks.en: Figure 1 : 3D contact volumes vs. 2D contact maps. Previous contact maps query points only on object surfaces, which can retain only a small fraction of hand surface. Thus it requires nearest-neighbor (NN) queries to avoid penetrations, which can easily stick in local minima. Contact volumes, however, sample points around the object surfaces and is able to retain the whole local hand configuration in the volume. Consequently, contact volumes can deterministically and precisely reconstruct local hand part and guide the pose fitting without instable penetration losses.
blocks.zh: 图1: 三维联系卷对二维联系图. 之前的接触图查询点只存在于物体表面,它只能保留一小部分的手表. 因此,它需要最近的邻居(NN)查询以避免渗透,而渗透很容易被粘入当地的迷你. 然而,接触量,取出围绕物体表面的样本点,并且能够在量中保留出整个局部的手配置. 因此,接触量可以确定和精确地重建出局部的手部并引导外形的相接,而不会造成不稳定的穿透损失。

blocks.en: Our target is to retain the fine-grained contact details from training data to the largest extent, thus reducing severe penetrations and improving geometric plausibility. Our insight is that the points to reason contact, i.e.,contact points, should not only lie on the object surface, but should be scattered around the surface. In this way, the contact can cover much larger area of the hand and preserve the exact penetration depth, thus no rules with NN queries are required. Further, as 3D grid representations [ 34 , 43 , 27 ] are limited by computational cost [ 25 ] , these points should be hierarchically organized to find the balance between computational cost and granularity.
blocks.zh: 我们的目标是在培训数据中尽量保留精细的接触细节,从而减少严重的渗透并改进几何学的可信度。 我们的洞察力是,理性接触的点,即接触点,不仅应该停留在物体表面,而且应该被分散在表面周围. 这样,接触可以覆盖手部更大的区域并保持精确的穿透深度,因此不需要NN查询的规则. 此外,由于三维网格表示[34,43,27]受到计算成本[25]的限制,这些点应分级排列,以找到计算成本和颗粒性之间的平衡.

blocks.en:
To this end, we introduce Vol umetric Co ntact (VolCo), a novel contact representation constructed from local volumetric grids whose centers are uniformly sampled on the object surface, inspired by Mosaic-SDF [ 42 ] . While Mosaic-SDF employs such local volumes to represent general object geometry via signed distance values, VolCo extends the paradigm to contact modeling of a fixed topology (hand) by capturing also the correspondences. Specifically, each point in a volume encodes the contact likelihood and the correspondence using Continuous Surface Embeddings (CSE) [ 28 ] . Furthermore, VolCo aggregates point-level features within each local volume. This coherent hierarchy allows the separate modeling of local configurations and global hand priors.
Based on the hierarchy, we present a volume-wise latent diffusion model i.e.,VolCoDiff, consisting of a 3DVAE i.e.,VolumeVAE and a latent diffusion model based on Scene Diffuser [ 15 ] .
blocks.zh:
为此,我们介绍Vol umetric Co ntact(VolCo),这是由当地量子网格构建的一种新型的接触代表,其中心在物体表面被统一取样,灵感来自Mosaic-SDF [42]. 虽然Mosaic-SDF使用这样的局部卷来通过签名的相距值来代表一般对象几何,而VolCo也通过捕捉函证来将范式延伸至固定地貌(手)的接触模型. 具体地说,一个卷中的每个点用连续地表嵌入(CSE)[28]来编码接触可能性和通信. 此外,VolCo还汇总了每个本地体积内的点级特征. 这种连贯的分级结构允许对本地配置和全局手前缀分别建模.
基于分级结构,我们提出一个量相潜在扩散模型,即Vol Codiff,由3DVAE即VolumeVAE和基于Scene Diffuser [15] 的潜在扩散模型组成.

blocks.en: VolumeVAE aggregates the common prior over local volumes conditioned on the SDF values, modeling what hand surface configurations are geometrically possible within each volume . Since each volume is small ( 2 3 2^{3} cm \mathrm{cm} ), the feasible configuration space is limited in scale and thus possible to be compressed to a compact latent code. VolumeVAE abstracts away the fine-grained surface geometry, allowing the diffusion model to focus solely on the global hand prior.
blocks.zh: VolumeVAE以SDF值为条件,汇总了常见的先于本地卷的量,模拟了每卷中何种手表配置可以几何. 由于每个音量都很小(2 3 2^{3} cm\ mathrm{cm}),所以可行的配置空间在规模上是有限的,因此可以被压缩成一个紧凑的潜伏代码. VolumeVAE摘要取出精细的地表几何,使扩散模型能够仅聚焦于全球手前.

blocks.en: The latent diffusion model is trained to capture what combinations of local hand configurations constitute a plausible grasp . This objective is governed by two key principles. First, all local hand parts must be reachable by a valid hand. To enforce this, an auxiliary branch is incorporated in the diffusion UNet to predict the hand pose, which is subsequently mapped to VolCo latent space to supervise the generated contact. Second, the grasp should be stable . Due to the joint encoding of SDFs and contact likelihood, VolCo allows the explicit contact force inference via a spring-damper model, and thus a force-aware stability loss can be applied [ 6 ] . Together, these two principles encourage the generation of physically plausible hand part combinations, while VolumeVAE ensures all local penetrations remain within plausible bounds. Finally, the generated grasp is obtained by initializing with the hand-branch prediction and subsequently fitting it to the generated VolCo representation.
blocks.zh: 潜在扩散模型经过培训,能够捕捉到当地手构型的组合构成一种合理的把握。 这一目标遵循两项关键原则。 首先,所有本地手部必须用有效手来取出。 为了执行这一点,在扩散UNet中加入了一个辅助分支来预测手姿,随后被映射到VolCo潜在空间来监督所生成的接触. 第二,把握力应该是稳定的。 由于SDFs的联合编码和接触可能性,VolCo允许通过弹簧护板模型进行明确的接触力推论,从而可以应用出出能感知到的稳定性损失[6]. 这两项原则共同鼓励产生物理上可行的手部组合,而VolumeVAE则确保所有局部渗透都保持在合理的限度内。 最后,生成的抓取是通过手部预测的初始化得到的,然后将其与生成的VolCo表示相接.

blocks.en: In experiment, we benchmark hand pose reconstruction from contact and compare VolCo with previous representations. VolCo shows the highest precision, indicating its capability to preserve the maximum hand information. We also benchmark the grasp generation capability on two public datasets, and our method achieves the highest stability, lowest penetration depth, and highest plausible contact area. It indicates the state-of-the-art grasping generation quality. In all, our contribution can be summarized in threefold:
blocks.zh: 在实验中,我们基准手从接触中提出重建,并比较VolCo与之前的表示. VolCo显示的精度最高,表明其保存最大手相信息的能力. 我们还将抓取生成能力以两个公共数据集作为基准,我们的方法实现了最高的稳定性、最低的渗透深度和最高的可信接触区。 它表明最先进的掌握生成质量。 总之,我们的贡献可归纳为三:

blocks.en: 1. We propose VolCo, a novel volume-based hierarchical contact representation capable of recovering the fine details of hand-object interaction; 2. We construct a VolCoDiff, a latent diffusion model for grasp generation that takes advantage of the hierarchical structure of VolCo by modeling local contact details using VAE and global hand geometry using diffusion; 3. We conduct experiments on pose reconstruction from contact and grasp generation, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on both tasks.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Contact Modeling . Contact modeling has shown great potential in hand-object estimation and generation [ 17 , 11 ] . Early approaches define contact as per-point likelihood on the object surface [ 11 , 17 , 36 ] , providing guidance on grasp location but leaving a substantial information gap to complete hand meshes. Later, the contact maps get enriched by including part / anchor label [ 40 , 27 , 49 ] , hand continuous surface embedding [ 28 , 44 ] , part orientations [ 24 ] , and contact forces [ 6 ] . Nevertheless, all such representations remain confined to the object surface and lack explicit modeling of penetration depth, leaving its recovery hand-crafted rules.
blocks.zh: 联系模式 . 接触模型在手对象估计和生成[17,11]中显示出了巨大的潜力. 早期的方法将接触定义为物体表面的每个点的可能性[11,17,36],为把握位置提供了指导,但留下了巨大的信息空白来完成手接网. 后来,通过包括部分/锚标签[40,27,49],手连续地平面嵌入[28,44],部分取向[24]和接触力来丰富联系图. [6]. 尽管如此,所有这种表述仍然局限于物体表面,而且缺乏对穿透深度的明确模型,因此其恢复的手工规则被留下。

blocks.en: 3D Hand-Object Representations . Some recent methods use implicit functions [ 19 , 5 ] or 3D volumetric grids (Bases Point Set [ 34 , 27 ] or SDF [ 43 , 5 ] ) to represent both hands and objects, thus relating them in a common feature space. Such representations effectively capture relations between hands and objects, but are limited in fitting to known templates or low resolution [ 25 ] . On contrary, VolCo is rooted on known templates and finds the balance of fine-details and computational cost.
blocks.zh: 三维 手拿开 物体说明. 最近的一些方法使用隐含函数[19,5]或3D音量网格(Bases Point Set [34,27]或SDF [43,5])来代表手和物体,从而在共同的特征空间中将它们相接. 这种表达方式有效地捕捉了手与物体之间的关系,但仅限于适合已知的模板或低分辨率[25]. 相反地,VolCo植根于已知的模板上并找到细微细节和计算成本的平衡.

blocks.en:
Human Grasp Generation . Human Grasp Generation methods have evolved significantly in recent years. Early methods [ 18 , 24 , 46 ] utilize cVAE [ 20 ] as the backbone, but are limited by the capacity and posterior collapse [ 1 ] of VAEs. Subsequent research [ 33 , 44 , 49 , 3 , 23 ] gradually shifts to diffusion models [ 14 ] , with latent diffusion models [ 31 ] recently taking dominance. The compressed latent space can reduce the number of parameters [ 49 ] and restrict pose plausibility [ 21 ] . Nevertheless, these methods lay their attention on global hand pose, ignoring the contact details.
Another line of work try to recover the contact first, then fit the hand to the contact maps [ 40 , 17 , 47 , 24 , 27 , 6 ] . However, due to the incomplete and non-deterministic nature of the contact representations, the optimization requires NN based penetration losses [ 32 ] and risks getting stuck in local minima.

人类巨星 近年来,人类格拉斯普生成法有了显著的发展. 早期方法[18,24,46]使用cVAE[20]作为骨干,但受到VAEs容量和后倒塌[1]的限制. 随后的研究[33、44、49、3、23]逐渐转向传播模式[14],潜在传播模式[31]最近占据了支配地位。 压缩后的潜在空间可以减少参数数 [49] 并限制产生可信度 [21]. 尽管如此,这些方法却让全球关注,忽略了联系细节。
另一行工作试图先找回联系人,再将手放入联系人地图[40,17,47,24,27,6]. 然而,由于联系方式的不完全和非决定性性质,优化需要NN基于渗透损失[32],并有可能被卡入本地迷你.

blocks.en: In summary, prior methods typically requires test-time adaptation with non-differentiable penetration losses for better generation quality. We attribute this limitation to the poor information preserving capability of existing contact maps, which VolCo is designed to address.
blocks.zh: 简言之,先前的方法通常要求试验时间的调整,并且为了更好的生成质量而无差别的渗透损失. 我们将此限制归因于保存现有联系地图的不良信息能力,而VolCo是设计用来解决的。

blocks.en: 3 Methodology
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: Figure 2 : VolCo and VolCoDiff framework . Within the local volumes sampled from the object surface, the hand mesh and VolCo representation are bidirectionally transferable. In each volume, a uniform grid is sampled, and each grid point encodes the contact likelihood and CSE, forming VolCo. Conversely, local hand configurations can be reconstructed from each volume using weighted average and concatenated to recover the hand geometry. VolCoDiff operates on the latent codes extracted from VolCo via VolumeVAE, with an auxiliary hand latent vector for supervision. The generated VolCo restores high-fidelity hand meshes around the object, with the hand decoder output subsequently fitted to VolCo to produce the final grasp.
blocks.zh: 图2:沃尔科和沃尔科迪夫框架 在从物体表面取样的局部体积中,手网和VolCo代表是双向可转移的。 在每个卷中,一个统一的网格被取出样本,每个网格点将接触概率和CSE编码,形成VolCo. 反之,可以使用加权平均值从每个体积中重建出局部的手相构型并被收缩来恢复手相几何. VolCoDiff通过VolumeVAE从VolCo提取出的潜在代码进行操作,辅以手潜向量进行监督。 生成的"VolCo"恢复了高纯度的手指环环绕物体,手指解码器输出随后被安装到"VolCo"中来产生出最终的抓取.

blocks.en: VolumeVAE encodes rich information about possible local hand configurations, so the next step is to answer: How to model the distribution of possible combinations of local hand configurations?
blocks.zh: VolumeVAE编码了关于可能本地手配置的丰富信息,所以下一步是回答: 如何模拟本地手配置可能组合的分布?

blocks.en: Latent diffusion models [ 31 ] has recently shown great potential in human grasp generation [ 38 , 49 , 21 ] . We follow this practice, but with one key difference: the latent space is the concatenation of the volume-wise latent code, following the global hierarchy of VolCo.
blocks.zh: 近代传播模型[31]在人类抓取生成方面显示出了巨大的潜力[38,49,21]. 我们遵循这个做法,但有一个关键区别: 潜在的空间是按沃尔科的全球等级来调和量子化的潜在代码。

blocks.en: To minimize the range of latent vectors, we set all volumes without hand vertices inside to zero, which are mapped to a constant latent. The resulting latent is a matrix Z c ∈ ℝ N × 128 Z^{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 128} . This volume-wise latent space integrates naturally with Scene Diffuser [ 15 ] , a point-conditioned diffusion framework. Inspired by [ 23 ] , we use the flattened Mosaic-SDF as the feature vector and utilize the PointNet [ 29 ] encoder to extract the per-point features. These features are used as the positional encoding in the attention-based UNet.
blocks.zh: 为了尽量缩小潜在向量的范围,我们把所有没有手顶的卷放入内部为零,这些卷被映射到一个常有的潜伏. 由此产生的潜伏是矩阵 Z c → → R N × 128 Z → c → in\ mathbb{ R}^{N\times 128}. 这种体积相通的潜在空间自然地融合了Scene Diffuser [15],一个有点条件的传播框架. 在[23]的启发下,我们使用平地的Mosaic-SDF作为特征向量,并使用PointNet[29]编码器来提取出每个点的特性. 这些特性被作为基于关注的UNet中的位置编码.

blocks.en: Auxiliary Branch with Hand Prior Guidance . Generated VolCo should be valid, i.e.,whether they can fit in a valid hand mesh (provided by MANO [ 32 ] ). Since the VolCo carries complete information to recover the hand, an auxiliary branch to generate hand based on VolCo latents is added. Also, to make sure the generated hand fall in the plausible manifold, the target is a latent z h ∈ ℝ 16 z^{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{16} extracted from an MLP-based VAE model. The final latent space is obtained by concatenation: z = [ z h , Z c ] z=[z^{h},Z^{c}] .

blocks.en: 4 Experiment
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: In this section, we conduct experiments on 2 tasks: reconstructing from ground truth contact and human grasp generation, both done on two public datasets.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们进行了两项任务的实验:从地面的真知灼见重建与人类的接力生成,两者都是在两个公共数据集上完成的.

blocks.en: Datasets . GRAB [ 34 ] is used as our training set and one of the test set due to its high quality motion capture data. HO3D [ 13 ] contains 10 objects from YCB dataset [ 4 ] and are not seen when training on GRAB. This dataset is used for benchmarking the adaptivity to out-of-domain objects.
blocks.zh: 数据集. GRAB [34]作为我们的训练集和测试集之一,因为其高质量的运动捕捉数据. HO3D [13]包含从YCB数据集取出10个对象[4],在GRAB上进行训练时没有看到. 本数据集用于对域外对象的可适性进行基准化.

blocks.en: Implementation Details . VolumeVAE and VolCoDiff are both trained using AdamW [ 26 ] with learning rates 2 × 10 − 4 2\times 10^{-4} and 10 − 4 10^{-4} for 20 and 100 epochs, respectively. Pose fitting uses AdamW for 1,000 iterations. Our experiments are done on a linux workstation with Intel(R) Xeon(R) w7-3445 CPU, 64GB RAM, and two 4090 GPUs. Please refer to Appendices B and C.1 for model architectures and data pre-processing details.
blocks.zh: 实施细节. VolumeVAE和VolCoDiff都使用AdamW[26]进行训练,学习率分别为2×10-4 2\times 10^{-4}和10−4 10^{-4},分别为20个和100个时代。 Pose装配使用AdamW来进行1000个迭代. 我们与Intel(R)Xeon(R) w7-3445 CPU,64GB RAM,和两台4090 GPU在Linux工作站上进行了实验. 关于模型架构和数据预处理细节,请参见附录B和C.1.

blocks.en: 4.1 Reconstruction from VolCo
blocks.zh: 4.1 从沃尔科重建

blocks.en: We test the correspondence and contact representations together with comparisons to previous representations on GRAB test set every 64 frames. Three criteria are utilized following previous research [ 48 , 13 , 24 ] : 1) End Point Error (EPE) —average Euclidean distance of mesh vertices; 2) F-score —harmonic average of precision and recall between vertices of two meshes under certain threshold(5 mm \mathrm{mm} and 15 mm \mathrm{mm} ); 3) Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) [ 9 ] expanding from 0 to 5 cm \mathrm{cm} . All hands are aligned to the objects. The resulting poses are obtained via optimization, initialized by the best 6D poses that fit the average hand to the contact. See Appendix C.3 for initialization details.
blocks.zh: 我们在GRAB测试每64个帧测试中测试函证和联系人陈述,并与以前的陈述进行比较。 在先前的研究之后使用了三项标准[48、13、24]: 1) 端点出错(EPE)——网状顶点的平均欧几里得分;2) F-分数——在一定阈值下两个网状顶点之间的精确度和回想率的谐振平均值(5mm\mathrm{mm}和15mm\mathrm{mm}); 3) ROC Curve (AUC) [9] 下的区域从 0 cm\ mathrm{cm} 扩展至 5 cm. 所有手都对准物体。 由此得到的姿势是通过优化得到的,由最能与接触相匹配的6D姿势初始化. 初始化详情见附录C.3。

The improvement from part labels to CSE confirms that point-wise correspondence is critical for reconstruction. The transition from map to volume representation reduces EPE by 40.1% at the same point count, highlighting the importance of sampling along the surface normal direction.

blocks.en: Fig. 4 illustrates the reason for improved precision. First, VolCo itself can recover local hand details without MANO as shown in the last column. This makes the fitted model precise at local details, restoring the slight penetrations; Second, as shown in ‘Fryingpan’ example, such contact encodes the exact spatial positions of more points with higher confidence around the object surface, which makes it possible to recover a tight grip around a slim bar—where the contact area is very small.

blocks.en: 4.2 Grasp Generation Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.2 干流生成分析

blocks.en: Metrics . Following previous research [ 17 , 24 , 38 , 6 ] , we utilize multiple criteria to evaluate stability, geometric plausibility and diversity of the generation. 1) Simulation Displacement (SD) measures the displacement of object center of mass in PyBullet [ 8 ] simulation; 2) Penetration Depth (PD) measures the average of all samples’ deepest penetration depth; 3) Intersection Volume (IV) is calculated by voxelizing the object meshes to 1 mm 3 1\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}^{3} and counting the overlapping voxels. 3) Contact Ratio (CR) reflects the ratio of samples in contact. To indicate the tightness of grasps, we introduce Contact Area (CA) to measure the valid contact area on the object surface (See Appendix. C.4 ). 4) Entropy and Cluster Size measure the diversity of generation.
blocks.zh: 度量衡. 经过先前的研究[17、24、38、6],我们利用多种标准来评价这一代人的稳定、几何学的可信度和多样性。 (1) 模拟迁移测量PyBullet[8]模拟物体质量中心的迁移; (2) 渗透深度(PD)测量所有样品最深渗透深度的平均值; 3)相交卷(IV)的计算方法是将对象中间体活化为1mm 3 1\text~,}\-mathrm{m}\-mathrm{m}^{3}并计算相重叠的活化体. 3)接触率(CR)反映接触中样品的比例. 为了表明抓住的紧凑性,我们引入了接触区(CA)来测量物体表面的有效接触区(见附录C.4). 4) Entropy和集群大小测量生成的多样性.

blocks.en: Quantitative Analysis . The results on both datasets are reported in Tab. 2 and 3 along with 1-sigma error bars. On the in-domain GRAB dataset, our method achieves the lowest SD and PD with the largest CA, exceeding the previous state-of-the-art by 14.8%, 32.5%, and 1.6%, respectively. This demonstrates that the generated grasps are stable, plausible, and contact-rich — whereas previous methods often collapse to similar poses in exchange for less penetration. On the out-of-domain HO3D dataset, our method surpasses the previous state-of-the-art by 12.3% (SD), 28.5% (PD), 18.2% (CA), demonstrating strong generalization to unseen objects. Despite HO3D objects being generally larger than those in GRAB, our method retains strong adaptability to these scales.
blocks.zh: 定量分析. 在Tab. 2和3中报告了两个数据集的结果以及1-西格玛出错条。 在域内GRAB数据集上,我们的方法实现了SD和PD最低,CA最大,分别比之前的先进水平高出14.8%,32.5%和1.6%. 这表明,产生的抓取是稳定的、可信的和富于接触的——而以前的方法往往倒塌到类似的地步,以换取较少的渗透。 在域外的HO3D数据集上,我们的方法超过了之前的一流数据12.3%(SD),28.5%(PD),18.2%(CA),显示了对看不见对象的强烈概括. 尽管HO3D物体一般大于GRAB中的物体,但我们的方法仍然对这些尺度具有很强的适应性.

blocks.en: Our intersection volumes are not the least among all methods, which is desired as a result of tighter grasps. Larger CA indicate that our method generate grasps with more valid contact. Since slight penetrations are allowed, larger CA is usually accompanied with larger IV. Over 28% improvement in PD on both datasets indicates a larger portion of penetrations are plausible. The preference for tighter grasps is also shown in Qualitative analysis in Fig. 5 .
blocks.zh: 我们的相交量并不是所有方法中最不重要的,这是由于更紧凑的把握而需要的. 更大的CA表示,我们的方法产生抓住 与更有效的接触。 由于允许轻微穿透,因此较大的CA通常会伴有较大的IV. 两个数据集的PD改进了28%以上,这表明渗透率的较大部分是合理的。 图5的定性分析也显示倾向于更紧紧抓住。

blocks.en: Qualitative Analysis . We compare our method qualitatively with previous state-of-the-art methods in penetrations [ 24 , 38 ] and stability [ 6 ] in Fig. 5 . The figure highlights the contact details, where previous methods tend to generate loose grasps due to aggressive penetration losses or implausibly deep penetrations especially in thin objects like wineglass and mug. This is due to the non-differentiable penetration loss with NN query. Our method, on contrast, finds a good balance of grasping steadiness and penetration—penetrations are common but mostly not severe, just like in the original motion capture data, indicating higher geometric plausibility. This also explains the lower penetration depth and higher penetration volumes, as our model prefers tight grasps with larger contact areas. More generated grasps are available in Appendix D .

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 4.3 读取研究

blocks.en: This section studies the contribution of VolCo and the key design choices, i.e.,hand prior guidance and explicit force-aware stability loss. ‘Prior Guidance‘ indicates if the auxiliary branch is used during training, while ‘Initialization’ means if the pose is initialized with the predicted pose. The first experiment use point-based contact maps following [ 23 ] .
blocks.zh: 本节研究了沃尔科的贡献和关键的设计选择,即手取先导并明确识别出力稳定性损失. `优先指导 ' 表示在培训期间是否使用辅助分支,而`初始化 ' 表示姿势与预测姿势初始化。 首个实验使用以点为主的相接地图,紧接后[23].

blocks.en: Table 4 : Ablation study on key design choices. The best are marked in bold and the second best are underlined . VolCo brings obvious improvement, and the stability loss is more effective in reducing SD with geometric plausibility ensured by prior guidance and initialization.
blocks.zh: 表4:关于关键设计选择的研究。 最好用粗体标出, VolCo带来了明显的改善,而稳定性损失在通过事先指导和初始化保证的几何可信度下可以更有效地减少自毁.

blocks.en: Point-based contact yields weak stability due to incomplete contact details and hand-crafted rules. Switching to VolCo ( 1 → 2 1\rightarrow 2 ) obviously improves stability. Adding prior guidance ( 2 → 4 ; 3 → 5 2\rightarrow 4;3\rightarrow 5 ) greatly decreases penetration depth, and increases IV and CA, while adding initial guess ( 4 → 5 ; 6 → 7 4\rightarrow 5;6\rightarrow 7 ) further improves stability and CA, highlighting the dual role of the auxiliary branch: it regularizes generated VolCo during training to allow being fitted by MANO with less penetrations, and provides better initialization during testing to fit larger contact areas. Interestingly, the stability loss reduce displacement obviously only when there is prior guidance ( 4 → 6 ; 5 → 7 4\rightarrow 6;5\rightarrow 7 ), suggesting geometric plausibility is a prerequisite for physical stability.
blocks.zh: 由于联系细节不完整和手工制作的规则,以点为基础的接触产生不稳定性。 切换到VolCo(1~2 1\正弦2)显然能提高稳定性. 增加前导(2 → 4;3 → 5 2\正线 4;3\正线 5)会大幅降低穿透深度,并增加IV和CA,同时增加初始猜测(4 → 5;6 → 7 4\正线 5;6\正线 7)会进一步提高稳定性和CA,突出辅助分支的双重作用:在培训期间将生成的VolCo规范化,使MANO能以更低的穿透度进行安装,并在测试期间提供更好的初始化,以适应更大的接触区. 有趣的是,只有事先有指导意见(4 ~ 6;5 ~ 7 4\正线 6;5\正线 7),稳定性的丧失显然才减少流离失所现象,表明几何上的合理性是身体稳定的先决条件。

blocks.en: 4.4 Runtime Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 运行时间分析

blocks.en: In this section, we analyze the trade-off between efficiency and performance against prior methods. Table. 5 reports a detailed runtime breakdown, with all experiments run on a single RTX 4090 GPU. Our method achieves the best simulation displacement and penetration depth among all compared methods. VAE-based methods need only a single forward pass at inference, while diffusion-based methods require iterative denoising, so the latter are slower. Among diffusion-based methods, ours has the second-fastest inference time. Its optimization time is also the second fastest overall, behind only the point-contact baseline [ 23 ] . Additionally, reducing the resolution from 128 × 8 3 128\times 8^{3} to 64 × 4 3 64\times 4^{3} has little effect on efficiency, suggesting the preference for the normal resolution.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们分析效率与业绩与以往方法之间的取舍。  Table表. 5报告了详细的运行时间分解,所有实验都运行在单个RTX 4090 GPU上. 我们的方法实现了所有比较方法中最好的模拟迁移和渗透深度。 以VAE为基础的方法只需要一个单向前传的推论,而以扩散为基础的方法则需要迭代去诺,所以后者更慢. 在基于传播的方法中,我们的推理时间是第二快的。 其优化时间也是总体第二快,仅落后于点接触基线 [23]. 此外,将分辨率从128x8 3 128\times 8\times 3}减少到64x4 3 64\times 4\times 4\times 4\times 3}对效率影响不大,这表明倾向于正常分辨率。

blocks.en: However, the point-contact baseline shows obvious drawback in batched inference. Although our method has more parameters (74.04M vs. 24.41M) and higher peak memory (358.1M vs. 191.4M), it achieves substantially lower TFLOPs (2.01 vs. 13.2). The major source of computation is the UNet attention blocks which scales as O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) in token count, not the volumetric representation due VAE compression. Thus our inference time barely changes as the number of samples increases from 1 to 10 (5.28 s \mathrm{s} → \rightarrow 5.47 s \mathrm{s} ), but the time of baseline increases substantially (2.90 s \mathrm{s} → \rightarrow 19.57 s \mathrm{s} ).
blocks.zh: 然而,点接触基线在分批推论中显示出明显的缺点. 尽管我们的方法有较多的参数(74.04M vs 24.41M)和更高的峰值内存(358.1M vs 19.1.4M),但它实现了大幅降低TFLOPs (2.01 vs 13.2). 主要的计算来源是UNet的注意块,这些块在符号计数中缩放为O Q(N)O(N),而不是应进行VAE压缩的音量表示. 因此,随着样本数量从1个增加到10个(5.28 s\mathrm{s} ~\ightarrow 5.47 s\mathrm{s}),我们的推断时间几乎没有变化,但基准时间大幅增加(2.90 s\mathrm{s}~\ightarrow 19.57 s\mathrm{s})。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We propose VolCo, a novel volumetric contact representation that faithfully preserves fine-grained details in hand-object contact. Building on VolCo, we present VolCoDiff, a volume-wise latent diffusion model, in which the local details are handled by VolumeVAE and the global composition of hand configurations is mitigated by diffusion. The experiments demonstrate the highest precision in reconstruction from contact and the state-of-the-art geometric plausibility and stability in grasp generation, emphasizing the value of introducing hierarchical contact volumes.
blocks.zh: 我们提议沃尔科, 一个新型的卷状接触代表 忠实地保存精细的细节 在手物接触。 在VolCo的基础上,我们提出了VolCoDiff,一种量论潜在扩散模型,其中由VolumeVAE处理局部细节,并用扩散来减轻手构型的全球构成. 实验表明,从接触和最先进的几何学的可听性和把握生成的稳定性来看,重建的精度最高,强调引入分级接触量的价值.

blocks.en: Limitations . Our method is currently limited in controllability and scale adaptivity. It prefers only tighter grasps, and the fixed number and scale of volumes limit the coverage of object scales. Future work will explore ways to control VolumeVAE latents and apply adaptive volume numbers and scales.
blocks.zh: 限制 . 我们的方法在可控性和可适应性方面目前是有限的。 它偏好只收紧抓取,而固定的卷数和尺度限制了对象尺度的覆盖范围. 今后的工作将探索控制VolumeVAE潜力的方法,并应用适应性体积数和尺度。

blocks.en: Broader Impact . Our method can help with improving AR/VR experiences and dexterous robotic deployment, but risks fostering the misuse of robots in harmful contexts.

blocks.en: B.1 VolumeVAE

blocks.en: VolumeVAE adopts a symmetric 3D VAE architecture, illustrated in Fig. 6 . The input VolCo and object SDF volumes are passed through two downsampling stages, flattened, and processed by residual MLP blocks followed by a projection layer to yield a 1D feature vector. Multi-scale object features are injected into the contact features at corresponding scales via channel concatenations. Due to the small input dimensionality ( 8 3 × n c ​ h ​ a ​ n ​ n ​ e ​ l 8^{3}\times n_{channel} ), the input is designed to minimize information loss: downsampling layers are implemented by 3D convolutional layers with a kernel size of 2, and all activations are LeakyReLU with a negative slope of 0.2.

blocks.en: The UNet of VolCoDiff is shown in Fig. 7 . The object SDF volumes are flattened to a 8 3 = 512 8^{3}=512 -dimensional vector, which are used as feature for each object volume center and processed by a PointNet [ 29 ] encoder. The hand branch receives the information from the object and the contact by cross-attention, while the contact branch does not receive information from the hand branch.

blocks.en: B.3 Hand VAE

blocks.en: C.1 Data Pre-processing
blocks.zh: C.1 数据处理

blocks.en: For training, we adopt the GRAB dataset [ 34 ] with the same pre-processing pipeline as GrabNet, yielding 323,622 frames of closely interacting hand-object pairs. The validation and test sets are obtained by downsampling every 4 and 64 frames, comprising 7,757 and 1,012 frames, respectively. The training set is used directly for training the diffusion model, and the test set is used in the experiment of reconstruction from contact. Further, the training set is augmented by a randomly selected rotation from all 24 axis-aligned ones which is applied to the local volumes. This keeps the rotated volumes still axis-aligned so no interpolations are needed. The resulting Mosaic-SDF and VolCo can be efficiently obtained by reordering the grid points.
blocks.zh: 为了进行培训,我们采用了GRAB数据集[34],其预处理管道与GrabNet相同,生成了323,622帧的密切相互作用的手-对象对. 通过每4个和64个帧进行下取样,分别包括7,757个和1,012个帧,来获得验证和测试集. 训练集直接用于训练传播模型,试验集用于从接触开始的重建实验. 此外,还从所有24个轴向相通的轮回中随机选择了适用于当地数量的轮回,从而加强了培训。 这样可以使旋转的音量保持轴向相通,所以不需要插入. 由此产生的Mosaic-SDF和VolCo可以通过重排网点来高效地得到.

blocks.en: However, the training of VolumeVAE requires special attention. The key concern is that one training sample of VolumeVAE should be one single volume with object SDF and contact values. So we construct a local volume dataset based on the sampled points. Each object surface is sampled 1,024 points, so totally 331.4M local volumes are available for training. The dataset exceeds the capacity of a compact VAE model, and a substantial portion of the data carries redundant or repeated information. We therefore apply two-level downsampling during data pre-processing.
blocks.zh: 然而,对VolumVAE的培训需要特别关注. 关键的关切是,VolumeVAE的一个培训样本应该是一个带有对象SDF和接触值的单卷. 因此,我们根据抽样点构建一个本地量数据集。 每个物体表面都取样了1,024个点,因此完全有331.4M个地方卷可供训练. 数据集超过了紧凑的VAE模型的容量,很大一部分数据携带了多余或重复的信息. 因此,我们在数据预处理过程中采用两级下取样。

blocks.en: To mitigate the similar poses between continuous frames, we downsample the training set every 5 frames, and validation and test set every 10 frames; To reduce the redundancy of nearby sampled points, we also downsample the object points each frame by 40% (training set) and 20% (validation and testing). Since in our VolCoDiff, non-contact volumes are set to 0, so fitting to those volumes in training is not necessary. Thus, we only take the sampled volumes with at least one hand vertex inside to construct the dataset. Finally, we arrive at a training set of 7,320,315 volumes, a validation set of 165,651 and a test set of 273,315.
blocks.zh: 为了减轻连续帧之间的类似外形,我们把训练每5个帧进行抽样,而验证和测试每10个帧; 为了减少附近被取样点的冗余,我们还把对象点每个帧进行40%(训练集)和20%(验证和测试)的抽样。 由于在VolCoDiff中,非接触卷被设定为0,因此与这些卷相适应的培训没有必要。 因此,我们只用至少一个手顶点的样本卷来构建数据集。 最后,我们完成了7,320,315卷的训练集,165,651卷的鉴定集和273,315卷的试验集。

blocks.en: To illustrate the process of pose refinement, we show some samples including the initial guess form the hand branch, the contact values shown in volumes, the segments reconstructed from VolCo, and the final fitted hand in Fig. 8 . We observe that the initial guess is usually closely related to the predicted VolCo, with only some slight displacement that results in artifacts. With the contact and repulsive losses defined in Eq. (9), the pose fitting stage efficiently converges to the optimal hand pose consistent with VolCo, for two reasons. First, The dominant loss term ℒ r ​ e ​ c \mathcal{L}_{rec} is essentially quadratic w.r.t. the hand vertex locations, yielding a well-behaved optimization landscape without the complexity introduced by contact calculations [ 11 ] ; Second, the initial guess provides a strong initialization in the vicinity of the optimal pose, facilitating the convergence to the global minimum.

Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [No] Justification: The code will be released upon accepted. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The hyperparameters are given in Methodology section, with brief motivations on choosing these parameters. Mostly, the hyperparameters are selected following previous works. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The results reported in the main tables Tab. 2 and 3 are accompanied with error bars indicating the standard deviation (1-sigma). Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The detailed computational sources are described in Appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: This paper utilizes only the public datasets for experiments, which are open-access for research purposes. These are no self-collected human data in our experiments. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The social impacts are discussed in the last section. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This paper proposes to generate the human grasp, which aims at studying the general interactive patterns and can hardly be used to harm public safety. Though it can foster the deployment of dexterous robots that might result in harmful context, this is more related with robotic breakthroughs and are out of scope of this paper. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The public datasets are properly cited and we use them following their terms of use. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This paper does not contribute new assets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: There is no user study in this paper. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This paper does not include crowdsourcing or research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: The main framework of the method is based on latent diffusion model, not LLM. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明: 本文的主要贡献是以本地卷为主的新型接触代表作和以它为主的抓取生成框架. 新方法可以通过更不严重的渗透来产生更紧凑的把握. 这在抽象和引言中显然是引入的. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明: 最后一节提出了这些限制。 • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应反思这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果该办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响该方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不包括理论成果. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 · 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明: 我们在训练和测试中使用的所有超参数都在纸上给出. 论文中简要地介绍了模型架构,附录中详细介绍了模型架构. B类. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 答复:理由: 密码一旦被接受就会发布 · 答案[N/A]是指纸张不包括需要密码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据和生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用的话)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 超参数在"方法"部分给出,在选择这些参数时有简短的动机. 多数情况下,超参数的选取是在之前的作品之后. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件的核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 主表格 Tab. 2 和 3 中报告的结果带有显示标准偏差(1-sigma)的错误栏. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-西格玛出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 详细的计算来源见附录。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 文件应披露整个研究项目是否比文件所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如,初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入文件)。 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 本文仅使用公共数据集进行实验,为研究目的开放查阅. 这些不是我们实验中 自我收集的人类数据 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和负面社会影响? blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.
